Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: Tax portal / e-services exist: Seychelles Nation explains SRC “taxation e-service” allowing employers to submit monthly payroll online via an e-service gateway (24/7) with e-ID/password/access code. Evidence is about e-filing/submission (payroll declarations) rather than full tax payment portal, but indicates an operational tax e-service portal.
revision_notes: Both cited sources (2011/2012) describe only a payroll e-filing gateway, not a full file-and-pay tax portal, so they do not support a code of 4 on the current scale. Fresh SRC (src.gov.sc) reporting shows the old e-service/e-gov gateway was closed to current-period filers from January 2024, with SRC stating it had 'started the migration process unto its new upcoming online tax platform' and directing taxpayers to lodge by bank transfer/email in the interim. The most recent SRC notice (30 March 2026) confirms taxpayers are still being 'encouraged to submit returns electronically via [email]... in addition to making use of the bank transfer facility for all payments', i.e. no live integrated file-and-pay portal with e-payment linked to the instant payment system is yet operating. A registration-only 'Seychelles Tax Portal' (tms.gov.sc) has existed since 2022 for obtaining a TIN, and electronic-filing regulations (S.I. 65 of 2025) have been enacted, but full online filing plus payment remains under development. Recalculated to 3 = Under development.
revised_comments: Seychelles Revenue Commission (SRC) has a registration-only online portal (tms.gov.sc) and has enacted regulations enabling electronic filing, and it has begun migrating to a new integrated online tax platform. As things stand, taxpayers lodge returns electronically by email and pay taxes via bank transfer to SRC's collection account at the Central Bank of Seychelles rather than through a single portal with direct e-payment linked to the instant payment system; SRC continues to describe the new platform as forthcoming rather than live.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: P2P functionality exists via both bank transfers (SEFT) and mobile money. Seychelles Nation reports Airtel Money (launched 2015) enables users to “load cash… send and receive money” via mobile. SEFT customer manual shows customers can create payments to customers of any commercial bank/SCU via SEFT.
revision_notes: The 2015 nation.sc article on Airtel Money's launch was verified and confirms P2P mobile money transfers. The cited SEFT customer manual PDF could not be fetched (repeated crawl timeout), so it was not used to support the score directly; a commercial bank's own description of SEFT (Bank of Baroda Seychelles) was fetched instead and confirms SEFT enables remittance 'to any Bank or to Seychelles credit union within Seychelles', supporting P2P bank transfer functionality. A 2025 industry overview corroborates that Airtel Money and Cable & Wireless mobile wallets continue to support P2P transfers. Score of 2 = Yes is confirmed on current evidence.
revised_comments: Person-to-person digital transfers are available in Seychelles through both mobile money and bank channels. Airtel Money and Cable & Wireless mobile wallets support P2P transfers, airtime top-ups and QR merchant payments, while the Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer (SEFT) system allows bank and Seychelles Credit Union customers to send funds directly to one another.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: CBS directly operates core payment infrastructure: CBS states it is “a payment system operator and banker to Government” on its AML/CFT compliance page, and CBS press communiqué on SEFT upgrade identifies CBS as “the operator of the system”. This indicates direct operation rather than only regulation.
revision_notes: The AML/CFT compliance page was fetched and confirms, in CBS's own words, that it 'is a payment system operator and banker to Government' executing payment transactions. The SEFT upgrade press release PDF repeatedly timed out on fetch and so is not relied on directly, but CBS's 2024 Annual Report (fetched via national assembly repository, confirmed to report SEFT/ECC transaction volumes for 2023-2024) and CBS's payment-system-modernisation page corroborate that CBS both regulates and operationally runs the national payment system, alongside its separate regulatory/licensing role under the National Payment System Regulations 2014. This is a maximum-scale code (5 = Direct Operation) and is flagged for human review per policy even though the evidence is judged to support it.
revised_comments: The Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS) both regulates the national payment system and directly operates core domestic payment infrastructure. CBS describes itself as a payment system operator and banker to Government, and its own annual reporting covers the transaction volumes of the Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer (SEFT) system that it runs, in addition to its separate role licensing and supervising other payment service providers.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Seychelles has an operational nationwide domestic electronic funds transfer system, SEFT (Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer). CBS press releases state SEFT was “officially launched on August 19, 2013 by the Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS), being the operator of the system” and enables domestic funds transfers; later upgrades integrated banks for straight-through processing (immediate debit/credit) and enabled broader customer access. The SEFT customer manual shows the SEFT service used by customers of commercial banks and the Seychelles Credit Union via https://www.seychelleseft.sc, indicating broad deployment.
revision_notes: The two cbs.sc PDFs cited in the original row repeatedly timed out on fetch and could not be directly verified; a commercial bank page on SEFT was read instead and confirms SEFT is a live, nationwide domestic transfer system. However, the metadata's own recommended primary source, AfricaNenda's SIIPS 2024 report (fetched and read), does not include Seychelles among the 28 live domestic instant payment systems (IPS) it catalogues as of June 2024; Seychelles instead appears only as one of the SADC countries the regional TCIB instant payment scheme is 'set to expand to', implying no confirmed live domestic or regional IPS meeting the near-real-time, 24/7 standard as of that survey. Separately, ProgressSoft's own description of the SEFT platform it built for CBS characterises it as a same-day, straight-through-processing EFT system for clearing 'within the same business day' rather than an instant (within-seconds) system, which is inconsistent with a 'fully deployed' instant payment system claim, notwithstanding a 2019 upgrade that enabled immediate debit/credit for some transactions. On balance, Seychelles has an established, nationwide bank-led digital transfer system (SEFT) plus mobile money, but the evidence does not support the top-of-scale 'fully deployed nationwide' instant payment system claim; downgraded to 4 = Partially deployed.
revised_comments: Seychelles operates a nationwide domestic funds transfer system, SEFT, run by the Central Bank of Seychelles since 2013 and used by all commercial banks and the Seychelles Credit Union for same-day, straight-through-processed transfers, complemented by mobile money services such as Airtel Money for person-to-person and merchant payments. A fully interoperable, near-real-time instant payment system meeting continental standards is not yet confirmed as live: AfricaNenda's continental tracking of instant payment systems does not list Seychelles among countries with an operating domestic instant payment system, and the regional SADC instant payment scheme (TCIB) is only planned to expand to Seychelles rather than already connected.
